label: H.R. 9609

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 19 - 16.

selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini.

summary: H.R. 9609, the "Less Bureaucracy, Better Student Aid Act," transfers specific federal student aid responsibilities, personnel, funds, and assets from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury. It requires the two departments to jointly set effective dates for these transfers in stages, beginning with defaulted loan collection, moving to non-defaulted loan servicing, and then encompassing other remaining student aid programs and administrative functions. The Office of Management and Budget must ensure there is no net increase in full-time equivalent employees across the affected agencies and certify compliance to congressional committees. Additionally, the bill terminates the authority to exempt delinquent or defaulted federal student loans from the Debt Collection Improvement Act.

affected_groups.effect: Personnel related to transferred student aid functions are moved to the Department of the Treasury, subject to rules preventing a net increase in total full-time equivalent employees.
affected_groups.group: Federal Employees at the Department of Education and Department of the Treasury

affected_groups.effect: Their loan servicing, repayment administration, credit reporting, and debt collection functions are transferred from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury, and defaulted loans can no longer be exempted from the Debt Collection Improvement Act.

key_provisions: Transfers functions related to the servicing and voluntary or involuntary collection of defaulted federal student loan debt from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury.
Transfers functions related to the servicing of non-defaulted federal student loan debt from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury.
Transfers remaining functions regarding federal student aid programs, lender and institution requirements, Pell Grants, direct loans, work-study, and other programs to the Department of the Treasury.
Requires the Secretary of Education and the Secretary of the Treasury to jointly determine the effective dates for these phased transfers.
Transfers all related personnel, appropriations, assets, liabilities, contracts, and property associated with the moved functions to the Department of the Treasury.
Directs the Office of Management and Budget to ensure no net increase in full-time equivalent employees at impacted federal agencies and to certify compliance to specified congressional committees.
Terminates the authority to exempt delinquent or defaulted federal student loans from the Debt Collection Improvement Act.
missing_information: Specific timelines or calendar dates for when the phased transfers are scheduled to take effect, other than requiring the agencies to jointly determine them.
Exact numbers or estimates of personnel and budget amounts that will be transferred between the two departments.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 9609, the "Less Bureaucracy, Better Student Aid Act," transfers specific federal student aid responsibilities, personnel, funds, and assets from the Department of Education to the Department of the Treasury. It requires the two departments to jointly set effective dates for these transfers in stages, beginning with defaulted loan collection, moving to non-defaulted loan servicing, and then encompassing other remaining student aid programs and administrative functions. The Office of Management and Budget must ensure there is no net increase in full-time equivalent employees across the affected agencies and certify compliance to congressional committees. Additionally, the bill terminates the authority to exempt delinquent or defaulted federal student loans from the Debt Collection Improvement Act.
summary_detail.significance: The bill shifts major operational responsibilities for federal student loans and financial aid programs from the education sector to the nation's financial agency, the Department of the Treasury. By consolidating these duties under Treasury and removing exemptions from the Debt Collection Improvement Act, the legislation alters how federal student debt is managed and collected at the federal level.
